static_traits.name: Xu Beini
static_traits.social_status: Social interaction is limited; only occasionally communicates with a few neighbors
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not received psychotherapy in the past; no similar psychological problems before

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling significant distress because plants she grows in the garden keep dying, and therefore concluding 'I am a terrible person'.
basic_info.core_demands: I realize that the thought 'because a plant withered and died, I am a very terrible person' is affecting my mental health and my ability to enjoy hobbies, so I sought counseling.
growth_experiences: After being widowed she has long lived alone in the countryside, with limited social interaction, only a few neighbors and little communication.

A few months ago garden plants failed to grow as anticipated and died off one after another; she tried adjusting watering schedules and changing plant types without effect, and began attributing failure to herself, feeling embarrassed and unwilling to share with neighbors; stress gradually increased, affecting daily life and gardening enjoyment.

core_beliefs: I am not good enough, cannot do things well

special_situations.event: When trying to tend the garden, sees the plants wither and die again
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot even keep plants alive, it means I am terrible as a person, very incompetent
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Frequently adjusts watering times and changes plant types, striving to prove they can keep plants alive well
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Why can I not do anything well? I am just a failure/a terrible person.

special_situations.event: Whenever preparing to start tending the garden, feels marked pressure
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the plants still fail this time, it again proves I am incapable, I am worthless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Continuing to change care plans (watering frequency, choosing different plants), trying to avoid failing again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time will probably fail too; I may be good at nothing.

special_situations.event: When reflecting on why plants died, ignoring environmental and external factors
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failure stems mainly from my personal flaws; acknowledging external causes could not explain my 'incompetence'
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Focuses attention on self-blame; gives less consideration to factors such as soil and weather
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: It is all my fault, I just cannot do anything well.

special_situations.event: When reviewing gardening results, mainly focuses on the withered plants
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only perfect care counts as good; any problem means I am very bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Filtering out one's efforts and possible objective conditions, reinforcing self-criticism
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: What I do is utterly worthless, with nothing worthy of affirmation at all.

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized as a capable person who can care for life and things
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being proven not good enough, judged as incompetent, thus losing self-worth and dignity
defense_goal: Gains a kind of 'sense of control' over failure through self-reproach and self-deprecation, avoiding seeking help from others in order to reduce embarrassment and the risk of being judged

object_relations.self_representation: An incompetent failure, someone unable to properly care for things
object_relations.object_representation: Bystanders who may judge oneself and embarrass oneself (such as neighbors / others)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked about the cause of a plant dying or facing plant-care failure again
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Directly equating failure with lack of self-worth, believing 'it is all my fault', reinforcing self-criticism (transference: internalizing external problems as self-defects)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expressing in a self-blaming tone, using absolute words (e.g., 'I am just incapable'), avoiding discussion of environmental or external conditions.

manifestations: Living alone in the countryside after being widowed, limited social interaction
Not sharing gardening troubles with neighbors out of embarrassment
outcomes: Interests and decreased enjoyment of life

manifestations: The once-loved gardening becomes a continuous source of stress and frustration
Overly binds individual worth to gardening success or failure, questioning self-meaning
outcomes: Experiences declining enjoyment of life and sense of meaning
Reduced motivation, avoiding sharing and seeking help

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Not sharing gardening problems with neighbors out of embarrassment
Not actively seeking external resources or support, turning stress into self-blame and internal friction

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Evaluates oneself with harsh labels (such as 'I am a terrible person')
Overly attributes failure to herself, limiting the room to explore external factors

positive_force: Has a certain willingness to act on the problem, has tried adjusting watering and changing plant types
Willing to seek psychological counseling and discuss thoughts openly
A few neighbors nearby can serve as potential support resources
negative_force: Self-labeling and overgeneralization, often evaluating oneself with global negation
Personalizes the problem, ignoring environmental and external factors (such as soil, weather)
Loneliness and embarrassment from living alone and limited social contact, reducing the likelihood of seeking help and linking resources

target_behavior.behavior: Significant self-blame and Anxiety around garden-care situations (negative automatic thoughts and self-deprecation)
antecedent: Seeing or realizing plants have withered again
When preparing to start tending the garden
target_behavior.core_reason: Over-binding plant success/failure as proof of personal worth, and reinforcing self-reproach and shame against the background of living alone and limited social interaction
target_behavior.function: Gains a 'sense of control' over failure through self-blame, while avoiding seeking help outwardly to reduce the risk of embarrassment and being judged
target_behavior.consequence: Interests and decreased enjoyment of life, daily life affected, further lowered self-confidence, problems spreading from gardening to Self-doubt in other areas
